note: Progress against the Phase 0 audit. Hand-maintained: mark items done only when verified, never when merely attempted.

items.title: Static test suite over the built artifact
items.note: 18 checks, zero dependencies, mutation-verified 7/7

items.title: Browser smoke layer
items.note: 10 checks in a real browser; proven to catch the never-laid-out map regression

items.title: Gate every publishing path on the suite
items.note: pages.yml plus all three data bots

items.title: Error telemetry and window.onerror
items.note: Local fault capture + one-tap report; nothing is sent automatically, and reports carry no location, saved places or key

items.title: LICENSE and third-party data terms
items.note: MIT for the code, DATA-SOURCES.md for the third-party terms; two ODbL/scraping questions flagged for a lawyer

items.title: Content Security Policy
items.note: Hash-pinned inline script, no unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval in script-src, per-directive host coverage enforced by the suite

items.title: Split the monolith into source files
items.note: 5,747 lines became 20 files in transit_data/src, concatenated into a byte-identical page.

items.title: Full ES-module isolation
items.note: Measured, then declined on the evidence. Zero collisions exist today, so the risk is unrealised, and a guard now fails the build if one is ever introduced — the same protection at a fraction of the cost. Conversion is genuinely feasible (the evaluation-time graph is acyclic; the only cycles run through function bodies, which ES modules resolve at call time), but it means exports and imports across 509 top-level names plus a bundler this machine cannot reliably install. Revisit if collisions start appearing, if more than one person is editing, or if code-splitting becomes necessary.

items.title: Shrink the 6.1 MB bus payload
items.note: Road geometry split into its own lazily-fetched file: the first bus interaction is 0.48 MB over the wire instead of 1.16 MB, and geometry loads only when a route is actually drawn

items.title: Per-record data confidence model
items.note: provenance.json declares source, licence, coverage and a confidence kind for all 29 shipped datasets; build.cjs stamps each file’s real modification time so freshness is measured, not claimed. Settings shows the list oldest-first, and the suite fails if a dataset the build reads is undeclared.

items.title: Close the 40 orphaned Istanbul bus refs
items.note: All 40 recovered: build.cjs reconstructs the missing directory rows from the graph, so nothing routable is unlistable. Ratchet retired for a clean assertion

items.title: Bring İzmir, Bursa, Antalya to Kocaeli’s level
items.note: İzmir done at operator depth: 441 ESHOT lines, 882 directions, 62,269 stops and road geometry, from the city’s own portal; stop ORDER derived by projecting each line’s stops onto its own route shape. Bursa and Antalya publish no reachable open bus feed — probed with İzmir as a control, evidence in DATA-SOURCES.md — so they stay rail-only by evidence rather than by omission.

items.title: Search ranking: match quality, kind, interchange, distance
items.note: Replaced “prefix then substring, each alphabetically” with a score. Adds Turkish names for all 35 English-only landmarks (“Ayasofya” found bus stops before), category words, prefix coverage scaling, interchange degree and distance as a tie-break. “havalimanı” now returns the three airports instead of a taxi rank; “sahil” moves rail from rank 15 to 1. Enter-to-resolve shares the ranking, so the list and the field agree. ~2 ms/query over 6,463 places. Open-now deliberately not added: no opening-hours data is shipped, so it could only be invented.

items.title: Widen local assistant intent coverage
items.note: Offline parser now answers the questions its own LLM tools already could: service alerts (“is M2 running” used to return a route summary, which reads as a yes), step-free/lift data per station, which rail lines serve a stop, and “how long from A to B”. All from data already shipped, EN and TR. Fixing the alert path also exposed a translator bug that rendered “istasyonunda” as “stationnda”; the missing Turkish case endings are now handled and every rule is  -anchored, so an unlisted inflection stays Turkish instead of becoming a non-word. Covered by transit_data/test/translator.test.cjs and 2 mutations.

items.title: Departure oracle with sourced confidence
items.note: Four tiers — published timetable > operator first/last/headway > published frequency > mode default — behind one synchronous API that always reports which it used. Exact timetables cover 18 line refs; Marmaray, M11, Metrobüs and every ferry have none, and the engine says so rather than inventing one.

items.title: Transfer feasibility and risk
items.note: arrival + measured walk + an interchange buffer scaled by how many lines meet there, compared against the real next departure. Verdicts safe/ok/tight/risky/infeasible, and deliberately NO verdict at all when the onward line has no timetable. No historical-reliability term: none is published, so it could only be invented.

items.title: Stop presenting modelled arrivals as live
items.note: The station board rendered “3m 43s” under a pulsing LIVE badge from the map’s decorative carriage animation. Now badged MODELLED, quoted to the minute with a “~”, and captioned with where the numbers come from. The exact operator board sits below it, unchanged.

items.title: Trip-match legs against the alighting station timetable
items.note: A leg’s run time is now read off the operator’s own timetables: two stations on the same line publish departures for the SAME vehicles, so the run time is the offset that aligns the sequences. M2 Şişhane–Levent resolves to 10 min at 99% support, M1B Yenikapı–Otogar to 13 min at 99%. Aliasing is the hazard — offsets a whole headway apart align equally well — so the search window is narrower than one headway and centred on a physical estimate; ambiguous or weakly-supported windows return nothing and the leg stays estimated. Arrivals that ARE matched let “missed connection” be claimed as fact.

items.title: Route by time, not just anchor to it
items.note: Dijkstra still runs on static weights and the clock is applied afterwards, so “arrive by” subtracts a fixed total instead of re-routing to catch an earlier connection, and what-if scenarios cannot be simulated. Needs a time-expanded search that preserves offline use. Two live consequences now visible: a plan across a shut line still quotes a boarding time (warned, and no longer claiming timetable confidence, but not rolled forward to opening); and route RANKING still uses static costs, so at 01:50 a route needing a 4-hour wait can outrank one running now.

items.title: Model rope-linked vehicles as a synchronised pair
items.note: Measured: F1’s two cars sit at 0.05 and 0.53 along the track moving independently. A rope-linked pair must satisfy posA + posB = 1, so they drift and can both reach the same end — physically impossible. Affects F1-F4 and TF1/TF2.

items.title: Expose the engine to the assistant as tools
items.note: The deterministic engine now exists; the assistant should call check_transfer / next_departures rather than reasoning about times itself. The brief is explicit that an LLM must never do routing arithmetic from memory.

items.title: Arrivals into a terminus
items.note: A leg alighting at a line’s terminus cannot be trip-matched: operators publish departures OUT of a terminus, never arrivals INTO it. Affects e.g. any M2 leg ending at Yenikapı. Deriving it would need a turnaround assumption, which is exactly the kind of invented number this engine refuses. Weighed and left estimated.
